mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past month signals an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS declines, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When unemployment exceeds 8.5% for two consecutive months, it signals labor market weakness that triggers Federal Reserve policy accommodation, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE > 8.5% for two consecutive months, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over a 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts and consumer spending indicate deteriorating demand conditions that trigger equity sell-offs, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when both HOUST and RSAFS decline, or interaction Rank IC remains below 0.03 over a 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Declining industrial production below 95.0 signals supply chain disruptions that reduce corporate earnings growth expectations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO < 95.0, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over a 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Rising consumer price inflation above 220.0 signals persistent inflation that prompts monetary tightening, reducing equity valuations and producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL > 220.0, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over a 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate increase above 0.25% in a single month signals monetary tightening that raises corporate borrowing costs, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 0.25%, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over a 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous unemployment above 8.5% and declining non-farm payrolls signal labor market deterioration that reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE > 8.5% and PAYEMS declines, or interaction Rank IC remains below 0.03 over a 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Strong industrial production above 96.0 signals robust supply chain conditions that boost corporate profitability, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO > 96.0, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over a 2-year window.
